sentences.en: Hello everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your Twenties, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our twenties,
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《二十岁心理学》（The Psychology of Your Twenties），在这里我们探讨二十几岁时经历的一些重大生活改变和转折，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello everybody, welcome back to the show, welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到本节目，欢迎收听本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, thanks for tuning in, it's so great to have you here.
sentences.zh: 新听友、老听友，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，感谢收听，很高兴能在这里与你相聚。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to cover a topic that's a little bit different from our usual content on this show, less relatable to our twenties, more of the psychology,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要探讨一个与本节目常规内容略有不同的话题，它与我们的二十岁没有那么紧密，而更多涉及心理学，

sentences.en: but I know that you all enjoy some of my more science-based episodes, so if you are one of those people, this one is for you.
sentences.zh: 但我知道大家都挺喜欢我那些偏向科学性的话题，所以如果你是这类听众，这一期节目正是为你准备的。

sentences.en: We're going to be talking about the psychology of dreams and daydreaming, where our mind tends to go when we are both asleep and awake
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨梦与白日梦的心理学，了解当我们入睡或清醒时，大脑倾向于去向何方，

sentences.en: and really dig deep into what exactly goes on inside our brains when we enter this nice, cozy, fantasy space.
sentences.zh: 并深入剖析当我们进入这个舒适美妙的幻想空间时，大脑内部究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: Dreams are like this massive metaphor, I think, and this massive concept in our lives.
sentences.zh: 我认为，梦就像是我们生活中的巨大隐喻和一个宏大的概念。

sentences.en: They show up in music, in literature, in art, in movies, all the time as this, like, incredible,
sentences.zh: 它们一直出现在音乐、文学、艺术、电影中，作为一种不可思议的、

sentences.en: imaginative landscape and symbol and metaphor,
sentences.zh: 充满想象力的景观、象征和隐喻，

sentences.en: but surprisingly, very little is actually known.
sentences.zh: 但令人惊奇的是，我们对它的了解其实非常少。

sentences.en: Very little is known about dreams, and this topic has been on my list for a while, but it just kind of keeps getting buried amongst some of the more relevant things
sentences.zh: 人们对梦知之甚少，这个话题一直在我的待办清单上，但它总是被我生活中一些更现实的事情

sentences.en: that have been going on in my life.
sentences.zh: 给渐渐淹没。

sentences.en: However, today is the day that we get into it and we give it its time in the sun.
sentences.zh: 然而，今天就是我们深入探讨它、让它大放异彩的日子。

sentences.en: Dreams are a really interesting concept to me, but also a really interesting concept in psychology because
sentences.zh: 对我而言，梦是一个非常有趣的概念，在心理学中同样引人入胜，因为

sentences.en: A, not much is known, but B, there are so many schools of thought.
sentences.zh: 第一，我们了解得不多；第二，这里的思想流派实在太多了。

sentences.en: Some say that dreams are our brain's way of sorting through information, of consolidating our memories.
sentences.zh: 有人说，梦是大脑梳理信息、巩固记忆的方式。

sentences.en: Others say that it's our subconscious coming to the surface, and there are some other really weird pseudo-scientific theories about future-telling, about what our dreams
sentences.zh: 另有人说，这是我们潜意识浮出水面的表现，还有一些其他非常古怪的伪科学理论，比如预知未来，或者梦境能够

sentences.en: can tell us about what we're thinking about and our repressed desires and what's going to happen to us.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们内心的想法、被压抑的欲望以及未来会发生什么。

sentences.en: Ancient civilizations, they used to think that dreams contained, like, certain prophecies, and it was
sentences.zh: 古代文明曾认为梦包含着某种预言，而且正是

sentences.en: Freud who came up with the idea that they are really our repressed desires coming to the surface.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德提出了这样的观点：梦实际上是我们被压抑的欲望浮出了水面。

sentences.en: So, some of these theories are obviously more valid than others, but what's also fascinating is how scientists and researchers have learnt to study our dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些理论中的一部分显然比其他理论更有依据，但同样迷人的是，科学家和研究人员是如何学会研究我们的梦境的。

sentences.en: We obviously cannot peer into someone's unconscious mind and watch their dreams from a computer screen, at least not yet, anyways.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们无法窥探某人的无意识心灵，也无法从电脑屏幕上观看他们的梦，至少目前还不能。

sentences.en: So, a huge amount of this research is based on subjective reporting, from basically asking people what do you remember and then people have slowly begun using things like
sentences.zh: 因此，这项研究的很大一部分依赖于主观报告，基本上就是询问人们还记得什么，然后人们才开始慢慢使用像

sentences.en: MRI machines and tracking our eye movements and EEG, but even then there are so many unanswered questions and they have found that everyone dreams, which is why this topic
sentences.zh: MRI（磁共振成像）机器、追踪眼球运动以及脑电图（EEG）等技术，但即便如此，仍有许多未解之谜，而且研究发现每个人都会做梦，这就是为什么我认为这个话题

sentences.en: I think will be universally accepted and loved and interesting, and a few different things kind of go on in our brain when this happens, which I really want to touch on today.
sentences.zh: 会普遍被大家接受、喜爱和关注，当这种情况发生时，我们的大脑中其实正在进行着几种不同的活动，这也是我今天特别想谈论的。

sentences.en: Some of those big questions still remain unanswered.
sentences.zh: 其中一些重大的问题依然没有答案。

sentences.en: We're going to do our best to answer them today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天会尽最大努力来解答它们。

sentences.en: Why do we dream?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么会做梦？

sentences.en: Why are everyone's dreams different?
sentences.zh: 为什么每个人的梦都不一样？

sentences.en: Why are they so illogical?
sentences.zh: 为什么梦如此不合逻辑？

sentences.en: What can they tell us about reality?
sentences.zh: 梦能告诉我们关于现实的什么信息？

sentences.en: And what is the deal with nightmares and lucid dreaming?
sentences.zh: 噩梦和清醒梦到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: We are going to explore all of that today, starting in the brain, working our way into our subconscious and out towards some of the major theories.
sentences.zh: 今天我们将探讨所有这些内容，从大脑开始，逐步深入到我们的潜意识，再延伸到一些主要的理论。

sentences.en: We are also going to cover the role of daydreaming as a little kind of side quest, a little bit of a bonus, a bonus episode within an episode.
sentences.zh: 我们还将探讨白日梦的作用，把它当作一个小小的支线任务、一点小福利，也就是一集节目中的“彩蛋”单集。

sentences.en: And although daydreaming isn't technically dreaming because we are awake, it's still incredibly important to cover and I think equally fascinating.
sentences.zh: 尽管白日梦严格来说不算做梦，因为我们是清醒的，但探讨它依然极其重要，而且我认为同样引人入胜。

sentences.en: I'm going to pop a little study in here, but there have been particular studies that have shown that we spend up to 47% of our time awake daydreaming.
sentences.zh: 我要在这里插播一个小研究，有专门的研究表明，我们清醒时间的整整 47% 都花在了做白日梦上。

sentences.en: So let's try and account for what actually goes on during that time because it's a massive portion of our waking hours.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们试着弄清楚这段时间里究竟发生了什么，因为这占据了我们清醒时分的大部分时间。

sentences.en: So what's going on there?
sentences.zh: 那么，那里到底在发生什么呢？

sentences.en: I've also been seeing this idea of maladaptive daydreaming all over my For You pages recently and I'm so fascinated by it.
sentences.zh: 最近我也在我的“为你推荐”（For You）页面上到处看到“适应不良性白日梦”这个概念，我对此着迷不已。

sentences.en: It's definitely something I have succumbed to in the past, so why not talk about it, particularly the role of daydreaming as a form of escapism.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是我过去也曾深陷其中的状态，所以为什么不聊聊它呢，尤其是探讨白日梦作为一种逃避现实手段的作用。

sentences.en: Without further ado, let's jump into the psychology and the science behind why we dream, including the unknown role and interesting role of daydreaming.
sentences.zh: 闲话少说，让我们一头扎进我们为什么会做梦背后的心理学和科学，包括白日梦不为人知且有趣的作用。

sentences.en: Even if you don't remember your dreams or you think that you don't dream, the chances are that at some stage whilst you're asleep, your brain has fallen into this imaginative
sentences.zh: 即使你不记得自己的梦，或者你认为自己从来不做梦，但在你睡着的某个阶段，你的大脑很有可能已经进入过这种富有想象力的

sentences.en: fantasy state at least three or more times and most of these distinct dreams last for like five to
sentences.zh: 幻想状态至少三次或更多，并且大多数清晰的梦境持续时间大约在 5 到

sentences.en: 20 minutes and the reason behind why this occurs has a lot to do with both our psychology and our neurology.
sentences.zh: 20 分钟之间，而之所以会出现这种情况，很大程度上与我们的心理学和神经学有关。

sentences.en: Dreams, they are essentially an involuntary hallucination that occurs when our brains are recharging and resting and they of course exist on a spectrum.
sentences.zh: 梦本质上是一种无意识的幻觉，发生在我们的大脑充电和休息时，它们当然也存在于一个连续谱上。

sentences.en: Some of our dreams can be incredibly pleasant and sweet and on the other hand we have people who are haunted by constant nightmares regardless of the content of your dreams, the
sentences.zh: 我们的一些梦可以非常愉快、美妙，而在另一方面，有些人则饱受不断出现的噩梦的困扰，但无论你的梦境内容如何，

sentences.en: same process actually occurs.
sentences.zh: 其实都会发生相同的过程。

sentences.en: So in general our brain goes through four main stages of sleep sleep and the main distinction between the first three stages and the final stage which is when dreaming occurs
sentences.zh: 总体而言，我们的大脑会经历睡眠的四个主要阶段，前三个阶段与最后阶段（即做梦发生的阶段）的主要区别，

sentences.en: is actually determined by what our eyes are doing.
sentences.zh: 实际上是由我们的眼睛在做什么来决定的。

sentences.en: That may seem a little bit strange that our eyes have something to do with this but let me explain it a little bit further.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能有点奇怪，眼睛居然和这有关，不过请容我进一步解释。

sentences.en: So stage one to three of sleep, they are all characterized by no eye movement.
sentences.zh: 睡眠的第一到第三阶段的共同特点是没有眼球运动。

sentences.en: So beginning at stage one, this only lasts like five to ten minutes, it's that like weird transition period between wakefulness and sleep and then we move into stage two
sentences.zh: 从第一阶段开始，这只持续大约五到十分钟，这是清醒与睡眠之间那种奇妙的过渡期，然后我们进入第二阶段，

sentences.en: where I think sleep like technically begins, our brains begin to slow down, our heart rate slows down, our body temperature drops and our brain starts to produce these really short
sentences.zh: 我认为睡眠可以说是从这里正式开始，我们的大脑开始放慢，心率减慢，体温下降，并且大脑开始产生这些非常短暂的

sentences.en: bursts of rapid activity as it shuts down and the next stage, stage three, this is where our deepest sleep occurs, this is where our body repairs itself and it is the most crucial
sentences.zh: 快速活动爆发，以此来关闭系统；接下来的第三阶段，这是我们睡得最深的时候，是身体进行自我修复的阶段，也是当我们谈论和思考身体自我修复与心灵自我重焕生机时

sentences.en: component of our sleep when we talk and we think about the body repairing itself and the mind regenerating itself.
sentences.zh: 最至关重要的睡眠成分。

sentences.en: But stage four is where all the action is really going on.
sentences.zh: 但第四阶段才是真正所有好戏上演的地方。

sentences.en: This is the showstopper.
sentences.zh: 这是一个全场瞩目的焦点。

sentences.en: Our eyes, they begin to move rapidly, which is why it's also known as rapid eye movement sleep, REM for short, and our brain activity most closely resembles our
sentences.zh: 我们的眼睛开始快速转动，这也是它被称为快速眼动睡眠（简称 REM）的原因，此时我们的大脑活动与

sentences.en: activity during waking hours because of course, this is where our dreams occur.
sentences.zh: 清醒状态下的活动最为相似，当然，因为我们的梦就是在这里发生的。

sentences.en: So we've gone through this, these previous stages of our brain and our body shutting down, but then when we reach stage four, REM sleep, everything fires back up, except
sentences.zh: 我们已经经历了之前大脑和身体关闭的阶段，但是当我们到达第四阶段——快速眼动睡眠时，除了

sentences.en: for our muscles actually, which become entirely paralyzed, which I didn't know that, but there we go.
sentences.zh: 我们的肌肉实际上变得完全瘫痪之外（这一点我以前也不知道，但事实确实如此），一切又重新活跃起来，

sentences.en: And we begin to have our most vivid dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 并且我们开始做最生动的梦。

sentences.en: You are most likely to remember your dreams if you are woken up during this period.
sentences.zh: 如果你在这个时期被叫醒，你最有可能记住自己的梦。

sentences.en: And interestingly, a study conducted at
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，一项由

sentences.en: Harvard Medical

sentences.en: School proposed that
sentences.zh: 学院进行的研究所提出，

sentences.en: REM sleep and dreaming during that time can be viewed as almost like a virtual reality that's been created by our brain.
sentences.zh: 快速眼动睡眠以及期间的做梦，几乎可以被视为我们的大脑所创造的一种虚拟现实。

sentences.en: In other words, we sense, we act, and we feel what we are dreaming.

sentences.en: The rapid movement of our eyes, which is now used to identify when someone is dreaming, it used to confuse people because they used to think back in the day, back in even as
